content.title: About
content.content: Boneless pork loin tenderloin is a lean cut taken from the back of the pig. It is known for its tender texture, mild flavor, and low fat content. Raw tenderloin is commonly used for quick searing, roasting, grilling, or slicing thin for steak‑style dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Tenderloin is the leanest pork cut, typically containing less than 5 % fat.
In the United States it is called “tenderloin,” while in many other countries it is simply referred to as “pork loin” or “pork tenderloin.”
Chefs often use tenderloin to demonstrate fast cooking techniques because it stays juicy without overcooking.
Raw tenderloin can be kept in the refrigerator for up to 3 days and frozen for up to 6 months.
Its fine grain makes it an excellent candidate for marinades, allowing flavors to penetrate quickly.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: A 100‑g serving provides about 20 g of complete protein, essential for muscle repair and growth.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: The low fat content makes it suitable for calorie‑controlled and low‑saturated‑fat diets.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Contains thiamine (B1), niacin (B3), and pyridoxine (B6), which support energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Provides zinc, iron, and phosphorus, important for immune health, blood formation, and bone strength.

items.title: Contains creatine
items.content: Creatine supports muscle strength and endurance, beneficial for athletes.

items.title: Food‑borne illness risk
items.content: Raw pork may harbor pathogens such as Salmonella or Trichinella; cook to an internal temperature of at least 63 °C (145 °F).

items.title: Sodium in marinades
items.content: If the tenderloin is marinated, watch added salt, especially for people with hypertension.

items.title: Meat allergy
items.content: Rare, but some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to pork.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Sear the tenderloin on high heat for 2–3 minutes per side, roast at 180 °C (350 °F) for 15–20 minutes, or grill it whole. Lightly season with salt, pepper, and herbs such as rosemary or thyme. For extra tenderness, marinate in olive oil, garlic, and lemon juice before cooking.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep raw tenderloin in a sealed container in the refrigerator at 0–2 °C for up to 3 days. For longer storage, freeze in a vacuum‑sealed bag for up to 6 months. Thaw in the refrigerator, not at room temperature, before use.
